fields.v: Liu, T., Guan, Y., Li, S., Wang, W., Yu, G., Lv, C. (2026). When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories. arXiv:2610.26394v1 [cs.SE], 19 Oct 2026. Code: https://github.com/TianqiLiu1/PACE-Bench
Preprint — arXiv:2610.26394v1 [cs.SE], 19 Oct 2026; no published venue stated
Zhejiang University (Liu, Li, Wang; Liu during an internship at Alibaba); Alibaba Taobao & Tmall Group (Guan, Yu, Lv), China — industry/academia

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark PACE-Bench (43 enterprise PRD-driven brownfield tasks, 750 expert-audited Code Points) with criterion synthesis, layered evidence-based evaluator and symptom-signal attribution, used to compare 11 model-scaffold configurations, knowledge-injection variants and three releases of the authors' platform harness

No named SDD approach; PRD-driven development as the task setting. Configurations: OpenHands 1.21.0 with GPT-5.6-Sol, GLM-5.2, Qwen3.7-Max, Kimi-K2.6, Opus-4.8, Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MiniMax-M2.7, Qwen3.8-27B; native scaffolds Codex + GPT-5.6-Sol and QwenCode + Qwen3.7-Max (versions not given). Authors' internal coding-agent platform harness releases v1, v2, v3 with Opus-4.5 (v1 organizes frontend work into clarification, decomposition, design and coding)

Agent input: a standardized PRD (prd/prd.md) reconstructed from production records, with sections goals, scope, functional requirements, business rules, technical constraints, acceptance criteria, open items; base repository. Hidden evaluation artefacts: frozen Code Points (acceptance criteria, provenance, evidence hints, permitted alternatives, weight)

Not prescribed for agents in the main study (instruction: implement all PRD requirements, inspect patterns, run relevant tests, inspect final diff). Authors' harness v1: clarification, decomposition, design, coding; v2 adds complex-task handling and subtask tracking; v3 adds plan-completion event. Benchmark: PRD reconstruction, bidirectional Code Point synthesis, expert review; evaluation L0 structural checks, L1 call-graph evidence localization, L2 semantic judgment, deterministic aggregation; symptom-signal attribution

None in agent runs (autonomous). Humans in benchmark: business-domain experts select cases and audit all 750 Code Points (56 revised or removed); three technical annotators re-evaluate all 750 verdicts on Qwen patches; engineers inspect diagnoses to revise the harness

Specification format only: a standardized PRD as the agent's task input; no SDD workflow run in the main comparison (harness releases add a clarification/decomposition/design/coding flow, evaluated only as whole releases)
Not classifiable (authors' wording: 'PRD-driven development', 'PRD-driven incremental development in enterprise brownfield repositories'; the PRD is a one-off task input)
fields.why: The authors do not use SDD terms, but their setting is 'PRD-driven development': a standardized PRD written before implementation is the agent's sole task input and is not maintained afterwards, which matches Böckeler's spec-first. 'Not classifiable' (the draft's value) is also defensible because no SDD tool or workflow is run.
fields.doubt: O PRD normalizado é escrito antes do código e é o único input do agente, o que se aproxima de spec-first, mas os autores não falam de SDD. Decide entre spec-first e not classifiable.

fields.v: Existing code bases: incremental PRD fulfilment (feature development) in mature enterprise brownfield repositories

43 tasks, 750 Code Points (median 16 per case); repository size median 120,616 code lines; PRD length median 2,799 characters; reference changes median 1,465 lines across 15 files (mean 1,749.93 lines, 17.58 files)

Enterprise e-commerce (Alibaba Taobao & Tmall): games & engagement 16, membership & promotions 11, product & commerce 7, content & discovery 5, engineering & data 4; objectives: business workflows 19, maintenance & testing 9, services & platforms 8, data & analytics 7
N/A (autonomous agents). Business-domain experts and three platform-side technical annotators, company employees in China; experience not quantified
None (no tokens, time or money for agent runs). Process counts per case: tool uses (59.8-122.8), verification commands, self-checks

Functional score Sc = weighted mean of Code Point verdicts (Covered 1, Partial 0.5, Missing 0), cases weighted equally, mean ± SE; success rate = share of cases with Sc ≥ 95 and zero Missing (complete delivery); point-level pass@k and pass^k, case-level success@k / success^k over 3 runs
Auxiliary code-quality observations (0-100), not part of the score: convention, architectural scope, naming-contract adherence, test delivery (on 9 cases requiring tests); syntax check 98.7-99.8
None in the benchmark. Platform rollout observation: mean requirement delivery time fell from 30.36 to 14.03 days (Feb-Aug), not controlled

Weighted acceptance loss by outcome symptom (contract/target mismatch, integration/registration gap, test-delivery gap, incomplete implementation); process signals from traces (verification gap, unretrieved files, error recovery); evaluator agreement (exact, weighted κ, severe inversions); execution vs judging variability; platform code adoption (monthly median 64.76% → 86.37%)

Automatic: frozen Code Points scored by L0 deterministic checks, L1 call-graph evidence localization and L2 semantic judge (Opus-4.8, default reasoning, 8,192 output tokens) with deterministic aggregation; process signals and symptoms by deterministic rules over saved traces and patches; quality observations by an LLM prompt. Validation: positive (reference patches) and four negative controls; agreement with a consensus of three technical annotators on all 750 Qwen3.7-Max Run 1 verdicts; three executions and three judging records for Qwen3.7-Max

Success criterion per case: complete delivery = Sc ≥ 95 and zero Missing; no criterion stated by the authors for a configuration, so quality and cost verdicts for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors. Values on 43 cases (score mean ± SE; complete-delivery rate): OpenHands 1.21.0 + GPT-5.6-Sol 78.08 ± 2.71, 14.0%; + GLM-5.2 68.80 ± 3.72, 9.3%; + Qwen3.7-Max 66.70 ± 3.45, 7.0% (three executions 66.70 / 65.44 / 65.37); + Kimi-K2.6 63.09 ± 3.79, 4.7%; + Opus-4.8 61.68 ± 4.39, 7.0%; + Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview 61.30 ± 3.84, 2.3%; + DeepSeek-V4-Pro 61.00 ± 3.65, 9.3%; + MiniMax-M2.7 52.13 ± 3.64, 2.3%; + Qwen3.8-27B 12.25 ± 3.12, 0.0% (17 empty patches); Codex + GPT-5.6-Sol 76.78 ± 2.81, 14.0%; QwenCode + Qwen3.7-Max 65.69 ± 3.83, 11.6%. Authors' platform harness + Opus-4.5: v1 59.37, v2 61.34, v3 63.04 (2.3% each). Knowledge injection, Qwen3.7-Max on 28 cases: no knowledge 58.54, locators only 57.80, repository-matched 59.23, shared long context 57.03

Tasks: the same 43 PRD tasks and base repositories for all configurations (knowledge study: 28 cases, 525 Code Points). Configurations: 9 models in a common OpenHands 1.21.0 scaffold (iteration limit 200, tool concurrency 4) and 2 native scaffolds; three harness releases with the same model. Baseline: none formal; paired scaffold comparisons, no-knowledge input as baseline for knowledge study, earlier release for harness study. Held constant: PRD, base, frozen Code Points and weights, judge. Acceptance: frozen expert-audited Code Points judged by the layered evaluator. Repetitions: one execution per configuration except three for Qwen3.7-Max. Human intervention: none

GPT-5.6-Sol (OpenHands) best: 78.1 and 14.0% (6 of 43); eight common-scaffold models span 26.0 points (52.1-78.1). Codex + GPT-5.6-Sol similar (76.8, 14.0%); QwenCode raises Qwen3.7-Max completion from 7.0% to 11.6% with a 1.01-point lower mean. Difficulty tracks the share of derived/implicit Code Points (75.0, 61.6, 56.8; ρ = −.410, p = .006, BH-adjusted p = .076) rather than size (|ρ| ≤ .083). Incomplete implementation and integration gaps account for 72.0% of weighted loss (65.8-78.1% per model). Static knowledge injection: −1.51 to +0.69 points (no consistent gain). Harness releases: 59.37 → 61.34 → 63.04 (+3.67). Execution variation 3.7 times judging variation (mean case SD 8.77 vs 2.36). No significance tests between configurations

Yes per the authors: controls separate fulfilment from superficial matches (reference 98.35, empty/unrelated/cross-case 0.00, identifier-only 4.03); full pipeline agreement with expert consensus 95.2%, weighted κ = .945, no severe inversions, vs 76.0-78.0% for judge baselines; judging more stable than execution. Repeatability of agent runs limited: pass@3 68.4% vs pass^3 33.2% of points. Limitations: consensus reference built only on Qwen patches; scores and diagnoses linked by co-occurrence, not causation; tasks drawn only from user-agent interaction records

Limitations: tasks only from real user-agent interactions on one platform, no other construction sources (e.g. merge requests); production PRDs, repositories and records stay under organizational access control; knowledge result limited to fixed inputs on 28 cases; process signals co-occur with symptoms without establishing cause; identifier-only control shows the semantic judge can grant structural Partial credit. Gaps / future work: extend diagnosis-guided feedback to knowledge evolution and targeted model training

Code (construction, evaluation, schemas, scoring, attribution) on GitHub; production requirement documents, repository snapshots and records not released (organizational access control). No pre-registration. The semantic judge (Opus-4.8) is also an evaluated model. Main-table Qwen result keeps earlier point judgments outside its targeted review, while the knowledge study uses new judgments (authors note the two no-knowledge means differ). Platform rollout metrics (adoption, delivery time) are uncontrolled monthly aggregates. Table 3 values read from a garbled extraction. Programming languages: Java (alone or with Groovy, SQL, HTML), TypeScript (alone or with CSS, JS), Python
